title: Roll out HTTP/3 without removing the escape route
description: Change discovery, network behavior, fallback, request safety, and rollout size. The route shows what the client can actually negotiate and which failure or replay risk reaches users.

discoveries.label: No HTTP/3 advertisement
discoveries.detail: TLS ALPN can still select h2, but this client has no route to an HTTP/3 endpoint.

discoveries.label: Alt-Svc from h2
discoveries.detail: The first response arrives over HTTP/2 and advertises h3 for a later connection.

discoveries.label: DNS HTTPS record
discoveries.detail: A supporting client can learn the h3 ALPN endpoint before the first origin request.

networks.label: UDP path works
networks.detail: QUIC packets reach the edge and the handshake can complete.

networks.label: UDP is blocked
networks.detail: A firewall or middlebox drops the QUIC path while TCP remains reachable.

networks.label: Wi-Fi changes to cellular
networks.detail: The client address changes during an established request sequence.

requests.label: Catalog GET
requests.detail: A cacheable, side-effect-free read can be retried after early-data replay.

requests.label: Idempotent PUT
requests.detail: A stable idempotency contract makes a repeated update converge on the same result.

requests.label: Payment POST
requests.detail: Without an application idempotency boundary, replay could create a second business effect.

earlyDataPolicies.label: 0-RTT disabled
earlyDataPolicies.detail: Wait for handshake confirmation before sending application requests.

earlyDataPolicies.label: Replay-safe requests only
earlyDataPolicies.detail: Permit early data only for methods and application operations that tolerate replay.

earlyDataPolicies.label: All requests in 0-RTT
earlyDataPolicies.detail: Lowest handshake wait, but unsafe operations can be captured and replayed.
